_comment: Versioned decision table for tools/route.py (docs/PLAN.md M2; references/docs/design/multi-method-consensus.md §2.2). First-matching-row wins. A row whose target has no shipped methods/*.json manifest yet (checked dynamically against tools/method.list_manifests(), not hardcoded here) is evaluated as a refusal regardless of its own 'then' -- see tools/route.py's SHIPPED-only gate. Rows R4 and R6 from the consensus doc's pseudocode are flattened into ordered sub-rows (R4a-R4d, R6a-R6f) so first-match-wins is expressible as a flat, testable list instead of nested branches; the flattening preserves the original evaluation order exactly.

then.note: a review update (Garner 2016): new protocol + PRISMA 2020 items 3/24 disclosure; NOT living mode -- caller must supply update_of citation

rows.source: goal ∋ update -> LIVING(base) if a completed base exists in results/<TOPIC>/ else ASK("which completed review?")
goal ∋ overview or evidence_type == existing reviews -> REFUSE{umbrella_review (v2)}; offer scoping_review

then.explain: describes reviews, does not appraise them

rows.source: goal ∩ {orient, prior_work, background} ≠ ∅ or question_focus == forming -> reconnaissance
goal ∋ map: evidence_type == algorithm/benchmark -> systematic_mapping_study if venue_default == cs_se
goal ∋ map: evidence_type == algorithm/benchmark -> else scoping_review if venue_default != cs_se
goal ∋ map: matrix dimensions requested -> REFUSE{egm (v2)} offer scoping_review
goal ∋ answer and question_focus == forming -> scoping_review, explain("your question is not yet answerable; map first")
rows._flagged: As literally ordered in the consensus doc, R3's own 'or question_focus == forming' clause is unconditional on goal, so it already matches every forming case before evaluation reaches any later row -- not just this one. R5 is the most visible casualty (always shadowed), but the same clause also shadows R4's map-specific sub-cases (a 'map' goal with question_focus=forming resolves via R3 to reconnaissance, never reaching R4a-R4d's algorithm/venue logic) and, most seriously, R6a's qualitative REFUSE (an 'answer' goal with evidence_type=qualitative and question_focus=forming resolves via R3 to reconnaissance instead of hitting R6a's hard refusal, which exists specifically so a qualitative question never resolves to anything but a refusal -- see the fallback rule below: routing must never fall sideways for a question type the tool cannot report correctly). Left exactly as specified (not silently reordered on a guess about intent) since routing behaviour decides which review type a reviewer is told to run, and for the R6a case, whether a qualitative question fails closed at all; flagged in the PR body for a human to disambiguate whether R3's forming clause should exclude goal ∋ answer and/or goal ∋ map.

then.explain: your question is not yet answerable; map first

rows.source: goal ∋ answer: evidence_type == qualitative -> REFUSE{meta_aggregation (later)}; offer scoping_review only -- never SR
goal ∋ answer: evidence_type == mixed -> REFUSE{mixed_methods (later)}; offer "two linked topics: SR + scoping"
goal ∋ answer: evidence_type == test-accuracy/model -> REFUSE{dta_narrative (v2)}; offer scoping_review
goal ∋ answer: evidence_type == algorithm/benchmark -> scoping_review or systematic_mapping_study (v1)

then.note: v1 fallback; v2 routes to systematic_review + structured_survey (pooling forbidden). venue_default reused from R4a/b as the same disambiguator -- not explicit in the source pseudocode, flagged for reviewer confirmation.

rows.source: goal ∋ answer: evidence_type == algorithm/benchmark -> else scoping_review (v1)

then.note: v1 fallback; v2 routes to systematic_review + structured_survey (pooling forbidden).

rows.source: goal ∋ answer: evidence_type in {trials, observational}: expects_pooling == yes -> systematic_review, family = pairwise_iv
goal ∋ answer: evidence_type in {trials, observational}: else -> systematic_review, family = structured_narrative (swim if rows are directional effects)

then.note: swim is a capture-time reclassification (directional-effect rows), not a routing decision

profile_offers.source: R7 profile offers (SR only), applied after the primary rows resolve a result

rules.source: time_budget == afternoon and goal ∋ answer -> reconnaissance ONLY, explain(...)

then.explain: you can find what exists today; deciding whether it works takes weeks -- here is the path to that if you want it later

rules.source: reviewers == 1 -> offer single_reviewer (verification sample menu); predicted label shown now
time_budget <= weeks -> offer rapid (RRMG shortcuts menu)

appraisal_intent_note.source: appraisal_intent == yes and RESULT in {scoping_review, systematic_mapping_study, reconnaissance} -> keep RESULT; explain(...)

then.explain_template: {method} does not appraise; if you need certainty claims you need an SR, which costs more

fallback_rule: Routing may only fall down the claims ladder (-> scoping -> reconnaissance) or refuse. It never falls sideways into an SR label for a question type the tool cannot synthesise or report correctly (qualitative, mixed, review-of-reviews, diagnostic accuracy in v1). A fallback is recorded as fallback_reason and printed verbatim in the manuscript's Methods.
